# edgeos_interface_ethernet (Resource)

Settings of a physical ethernet port (`interfaces ethernet <name>`). The port must already exist; creating the resource takes it over and never creates or deletes the interface itself.

Only the attributes you set are managed. Anything you leave out (and every option this resource does not model, such as `pppoe`, `poe` or `bridge-group`) is neither read nor changed. VLAN subinterfaces are managed with `edgeos_interface_vif` and are never touched. Removing an attribute from the configuration removes that setting from the port. Import reads every modelled setting the port has.

Destroying the resource removes the settings it manages from the port and keeps the port. `duplex` and `speed` cannot be removed from a physical port, so destroy sets both back to `auto`. Removing `addresses` or `firewall_*` from a port you reach the router through can cut you off.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "edgeos_firewall_name" "wan_in" {
  name = "WAN_IN"
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_name" "wan_local" {
  name = "WAN_LOCAL"
}

# The WAN port gets its address from the ISP and is protected by two rule sets.
resource "edgeos_interface_ethernet" "wan" {
  name           = "eth0"
  description    = "ISP uplink"
  addresses      = ["dhcp"]
  firewall_in    = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_in.name
  firewall_local = edgeos_firewall_name.wan_local.name

  dhcp_options = {
    default_route          = true
    default_route_distance = 210
    name_server            = false
  }
}

# A LAN port with static addresses and a fixed link.
resource "edgeos_interface_ethernet" "lan" {
  name        = "eth1"
  description = "LAN"
  addresses   = ["192.168.1.1/24", "2001:db8:1::1/64"]
  duplex      = "full"
  speed       = "1000"
  mtu         = 1500
}

# An unused port, switched off.
resource "edgeos_interface_ethernet" "spare" {
  name     = "eth4"
  disabled = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Interface name, such as `eth0`. The port has to exist on the router. Changing it manages a different port.

### Optional

- `addresses` (Set of String) Addresses of the port: addresses with prefix length such as `192.0.2.1/24` or `2001:db8::1/64`, or `dhcp` / `dhcpv6` to use a DHCP client.
- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `dhcp_options` (Attributes) DHCP client options, used with `addresses = ["dhcp"]`. Client and global options (`client-option`, `global-option`) are not managed here and are left alone. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dhcp_options))
- `disabled` (Boolean) `true` switches the port off (the `disable` node), `false` makes sure it is on. Leave it unset to not manage it.
- `duplex` (String) `auto`, `half` or `full`. Set `duplex` and `speed` together: both `auto`, or both fixed. When unset, Terraform reads the value from the port and leaves it alone.
- `firewall_in` (String) Name of the IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic coming in on the interface and forwarded (`firewall in name`). The rule set has to exist, usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`; EdgeOS refuses the commit otherwise.
- `firewall_local` (String) Name of the IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic coming in on the interface for the router itself (`firewall local name`). The rule set has to exist, usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`; EdgeOS refuses the commit otherwise.
- `firewall_out` (String) Name of the IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic forwarded out of the interface (`firewall out name`). The rule set has to exist, usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`; EdgeOS refuses the commit otherwise.
- `mac` (String) MAC address to use instead of the hardware address, in lower case.
- `mtu` (Number) MTU from 68 to 9000. The hardware may support less.
- `speed` (String) `auto`, `10`, `100`, `1000` or `10000` (Mbit/s). Set `duplex` and `speed` together: both `auto`, or both fixed. When unset, Terraform reads the value from the port and leaves it alone.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The interface name.

<a id="nestedatt--dhcp_options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dhcp_options`

Optional:

- `default_route` (Boolean) Install the default route the DHCP server hands out. `true` writes `update`, `false` writes `no-update`.
- `default_route_distance` (Number) Administrative distance of the default route learned from DHCP, from 1 to 255.
- `name_server` (Boolean) Use the DNS servers the DHCP server hands out. `true` writes `update`, `false` writes `no-update`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_interface_ethernet.example 'eth0'
```
